about: The pictures of promo edit 1, the Light. Every file was fetched from Wikimedia Commons on 2026-11-23 at the width given ('fetched_width'); 'licence' is what that page states. A statue's photograph is the museum's own, released CC0 under its Open Access policy (The Met's own record marks each isPublicDomain: true; 'museum_page' is that record). The icons and the painting are faithful photographs of flat works long out of copyright, marked Public domain on Commons. None is held in Greece or Italy (lib/marketing/heritagePictures.ts). 'eyes' is where the eyes are in the fetched file, read off by hand: the eye at the viewer's left first. The files themselves are out of git. From 2026-11-24, at his word that the pagans can be any kind of picture, the run also takes old engravings: flat printed works long out of copyright, marked Public domain on Commons. They are ink already and are not put through the ink filter. 'focus' is the point of the print that is held, as shares of its width and height.

saul.what: The Conversion of Saint Paul, by Parmigianino, oil on canvas, about 1527
saul.used: the light: Saul alone, cut out whole from the ground, the horse and the landscape left out

adramelech.what: Adramelech (2 Kings 17:31), engraving after Louis Le Breton, from Collin de Plancy's Dictionnaire infernal, Paris, 1863
adramelech.held: A printed book (the copy shown is the Bibliothèque nationale de France's, on Gallica)

dagon.what: The fish-god of Nimrud, called Dagon (1 Samuel 5:2), wood engraving after Layard's drawing, from Illustrerad verldshistoria, Stockholm, 1875
